The risk neutrality aspect is also relevant. It suggests I'm willing to take chances for potentially higher rewards. In this context, a slightly less truthful ranking could increase my chances of getting into a good school, even if it's not my absolute top choice.

I will therefore rank w > y > x > z. This is still very close to my true preference order, and preserves my high priority at w and y. It attempts to capitalize on the likely applicant pool dynamics.
